Vi søger en servicemedarbejder til Boligforeningen 3B – en god kollega, der trives med ansvar, struktur og kontakt til mange forskellige mennesker. Du får en central rolle i arbejdet med ind- og fraflytningssyn og bliver en vigtig del af den fortsatte udvikling af synsarbejdet. Flere boligafdelinger står over for større helhedsplaner i de kommende år, herunder Folehaven, som skal gennemgå en omfattende udvikling. Du bliver en del af en arbejdsplads, hvor vi ikke bare har trivslen men også det gode fællesskab, lederskab og kollegaskab tilfælles. Bliv nøgleperson i synsarbejdet Du får en selvstændig og alsidig hverdag. Du bliver samtidig en del af et engageret team, hvor vi hjælper hinanden og deler vores viden. Du gennemfører ind- og fraflytningssyn. Du udarbejder synsrapporter og sikrer korrekt dokumentation. Du koordinerer istandsættelsesarbejder og følger op på sager. Du samarbejder med beboere, håndværkere og kolleger. Du løser administrative opgaver i forbindelse med syn. Du bidrager til ensartede arbejdsgange og høj kvalitet. Du er med til at sikre gode flytteforløb for beboerne. Du passer godt ind, hvis: Du har minimum 10 års erfaring med ind- og fraflytningssyn. Du har solid erfaring med syn af almene boliger. Du har en god administrativ forståelse. Du arbejder struktureret og selvstændigt. Du er serviceminded og imødekommende. Du samarbejder godt med både beboere, kolleger og håndværkere. Du tager ansvar og leverer høj kvalitet. Arbejdstid og arbejdssted Stillingen er på fuld tid, og arbejdsstedet er Folehaven 7, 2500 Valby, og opgaverne løses på tværs af boligafdelinger i Valby og Sydhavn. Ønsker du at høre mere? Du er velkommen til at kontakte serviceleder Christina Mikkelsen på telefon 24 75 54 15 eller mail chrmi@kab-bolig.dk . Send din ansøgning senest den 10. august 2026. Vi afholder samtaler løbende og ansætter, når vi har fundet den rette kandidat. Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig. At the Copenhagen Institute for Futures Studies, we view foresight as a powerful capability—one that equips organisations and individuals to navigate complexity, anticipate change, and make more informed strategic decisions. We believe that futures capability arises from the understanding that the world is uncertain: there is not one extrapolated future, but many possible futures, and foresight offers tools to address the uncertainty this brings. As such, it is both a mindset and a set of skills, processes, and competencies that enable an organisation to act effectively in response to change or uncertainty. By applying a futures lens to the present, foresight enhances your capacity to question prevailing assumptions, detect emerging trends, and think beyond linear or short-term solutions. It cultivates the skills needed to identify patterns of change, surface strategic blind spots, and develop flexible, resilient responses to uncertainty. As AI and technology becomes increasingly embedded in everything from infrastructure to our imagination, the critical questions we need to ask becomes even more relevant: What’s human, what’s machine - and how do we navigate the entangled, uncertain futures in between? At the Copenhagen Institute for Futures Studies, we explore the messy middle. We're exploring both the spark of innovation, and the ripple effects it sends through society, culture and democracy. Because here’s the thing: technology and AI aren't good or bad. But they’re definitely not neutral either. They mirror our choices, our values - and sometimes, our blind spots. That’s why we use futures thinking to unpack how ethics, immersive interfaces and Agentic AI connect in unexpected (and sometimes unsettling) ways. As part of our agenda, we also explore how the future of media - increasingly liquid, synthetic, and generative - both mirrors and amplifies societal shifts, shaping an AI-mediated information ecosystem of tomorrow. This is not about predicting the future. It’s about being prepared –with nuance, intention, and a healthy dose of curiosity. Our mission is to drive a positive urban transformation by generating ideas, knowledge, prototypes, and strategies that promote equitable, resilient, and liveable cities. Our cities today stand for an emerging global governing force that is essential to addressing some of the world's most pressing challenges. In practical terms, we define futures impact as the change that occurs when people and organisations gain clearer insight into possible futures, enabling them to make informed choices today and actively shape the systems they are part of. When CIFS equips key actors with futures literacy, practical methods, and shared spaces for imagination and strategy, individuals gain agency, organisations embed foresight in decisions, and coalitions influence narratives, policy, and institutional direction — contributing over time to more resilient, and future-ready societal systems. CIFS’ tiered theory of change is built across three interconnected levels, each reinforcing different uses of the future to inform the present: Change in people: Future-oriented mindsets and skills that support long-term perspectives, new understandings of agency, imagination of alternatives, and more intentional action in the present. Change in communities and organisations: Embedding foresight in everyday practices fosters a shared language and sensemaking, leading to clearer strategic choices and stronger capabilities in areas such as innovation, risk, strategy and change management.
